item.title: US stocks today: US stocks turn choppy as megacaps offset chip gains before Fed meet
item.description: In the US stock market, a mixed performance emerged as chipmakers like Micron Technology surged, buoyed by favorable reports from SK Hynix, while major tech players such as Tesla and Apple faced declines. Investors eye the Federal Reserve's imminent interest rate decision and important earnings announcements from Microsoft and Alphabet. The Nasdaq showed positive momentum this week, rising around 2%, reflecting growing optimism surrounding artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US stocks traded in a narrow range on Wednesday as gains in chipmakers following strong results from South Korea's SK Hynix were offset by declines in heavyweight technology stocks, with investors awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and key earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet, Reuters reported.At 10:01 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 73.40 points, or 0.14%, at 52,450.97. The S&P 500 gained 0.09% to 7,729.20, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.03% to 26,470.68, according to Reuters. For live updates on US Markets, click here Chip stocks rally on SK Hynix resultsMemory chipmaker Micron Technology rose 4.8% to its highest level in more than two weeks after SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold jump in quarterly profit. SK Hynix's US listed shares surged 10.6%, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index gained 0.9%, putting it on track for a fourth straight session of gains, Reuters said.The strength in chips was partly offset by losses in megacaps. Tesla fell 1.9% after gaining more than 9% over the previous two sessions, while Apple slipped 0.6%. SpaceX dropped 3.2%.Alphabet rose 1.2% after a media report said OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips.Fed, AI spending and hyperscaler earnings in focusThe Nasdaq has gained about 2% this week as sentiment around artificial intelligence improved following Anthropic's US IPO filing on Monday. Attention now turns to Microsoft and Alphabet, which are due to report quarterly results after the closing bell, Reuters reported.Investors are expected to focus on cloud growth and capital spending, particularly whether heavy AI investments are generating sufficient returns. Concerns over debt funded AI spending remain a drag on sentiment as borrowing costs rise. We can still see that the AI demand has not paused... the number one worry for investors is not AI valuations anymore, but it's the financing through debt as debt goes through the roof in the US, said Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group.The Fed's policy announcement is due at 2 p.m. ET, with markets broadly expecting a pause after last month's hike. Investors are likely to focus on Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments and the policy outlook, Reuters reported. (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Tuborg maker Carlsberg India moves closer to IPO, files updated DRHP for complete OFS issue
item.description: Carlsberg India has filed an updated draft prospectus with Sebi for an IPO comprising 8.64 crore shares, entirely through an offer for sale by existing shareholders. The Tuborg maker could raise up to $700 million, according to earlier reports, as multinational companies increasingly tap India’s equity markets to monetise local businesses.
item.dc:creator: Akash Podishetti
item.content:encoded: Danish brewing giant Carlsberg's Indian subsidiary has moved closer to its stock market debut after filing an updated draft prospectus with market regulator Sebi for an initial public offering (IPO) comprising 8.64 crore shares, joining a growing list of multinational companies seeking to unlock the value of their Indian businesses.The proposed offering will consist entirely of an offer for sale (OFS) of 86.42 million equity shares by existing shareholders, according to the updated draft red herring prospectus dated October 27.Since the issue is entirely an OFS, Carlsberg India will receive no proceeds from the share sale. The money raised will go to the selling shareholder.The company has yet to announce its IPO price band, subscription dates or the total amount it intends to raise.Carlsberg India had initially submitted its IPO documents through Sebi's confidential filing route in July 2026. The regulator cleared the pre-filing earlier this month, allowing the company to proceed with the public filing.According to earlier Bloomberg reports, the offering could raise as much as $700 million, with the company considering a launch as early as December, subject to market conditions.The company has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India and JP Morgan India as book-running lead managers.Carlsberg India's planned listing comes amid growing interest from multinational companies in India's equity markets, where valuations have encouraged foreign parents to sell stakes in their local subsidiaries.South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor raised Rs 27,870 crore through its Indian subsidiary's IPO in October 2024, which was then the country's largest public offering. LG Electronics India followed with an Rs 11,607 crore IPO in October 2025, allowing its South Korean parent to monetise part of its investment in the Indian consumer electronics business.Both offerings were structured entirely as offers for sale. Carlsberg is now looking to follow a similar route, offering public market investors an opportunity to own shares in one of India's largest brewing companies.Also read | No. 2 on Day 1: How Jio Platforms broke India’s market cap hierarchy in debut tradeThe proposed issue also comes during a busy period for India's primary market. Jio Platforms made its stock market debut on Wednesday following its Rs 30,188 crore IPO, the largest in India's history. The offering was subscribed 22.19 times and attracted public bids worth Rs 4.9 lakh crore.About Carlsberg IndiaCarlsberg India is one of the country's leading brewing companies, competing with United Breweries, which markets the Kingfisher brand.The company entered India in 2007 and markets beer brands including Tuborg, Carlsberg Elephant and Kronenbourg 1664 Blanc.According to its updated prospectus, Carlsberg India operates seven company-owned breweries and works with nine third-party manufacturers across the country.The company reported a market share of 21.9% across 16 key states and union territories, reflecting its position in India's beer market.Its operations cover different beer categories, including mainstream, strong and premium offerings. Carlsberg India's listed peers include United Breweries, United Spirits, Radico Khaitan and Allied Blenders and Distillers.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
